# Best RV power station and solar combos

The search results don't include bundle prices, so I'm pairing stations with panels myself. Match the panels to the station's maximum solar input, since a station can't take more than that.

## My picks

**1. Best value for a big RV setup: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, with a dedicated RV outlet.
- Accepts up to 2,000 W of solar over three inputs (650 W each), so it can use a large panel array.
- Store price is $1,499. With code ALLPOWERS26 or EXTRA10 it's $1,349.10, and EXTRA12 brings it to $1,319.12. EXTRA10 and EXTRA12 expire 2026-11-15 and ALLPOWERS26 expires 2026-12-30. Only one code works per order.
- Caveats:
  - It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install than a portable unit.
  - You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W.
  - Buyers pay return shipping, and sale items may not be returnable.
  - The warranty is 5 years.
- [Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. [Source](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

**2. Best all-round for full-timers and boondockers: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous and 8,000 W surge, expandable past 12 kWh.
- Recharges 0–80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet, and runs under 30 dBA at light load.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and the most expensive once you add batteries.
- It can run a 13,500 BTU roof AC for about 2.3 hours. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- The results don't list its solar input or current price. Check both before you size panels.

**3. Best mid-range with an RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, built-in 30A RV outlet, and up to 1,200 W solar input.
- It weighs about 62 lb. [Sources](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) and [here](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- Bluetti is generally the cheapest per watt-hour, but its support is rated weakest of the big three. [Source](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**4. Best for weekend trips: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**
- 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W, and only about 23.8 lb.
- Solar input is capped at 400 W, so two SolarSaga 200 W panels is the most it can use. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- It's enough for a fridge, Starlink and a laptop, but not an air conditioner.

## Solar panels
- **Weekend or small rigs:** foldable panels in the 200–400 W range work well. A 300–400 W folding array refills a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Panel models:** one guide suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase and a 100W foldable panel as pairings for smaller units. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) Jackery's own SolarSaga 100 W and 200 W panels are the natural match for Jackery stations.
- **Rooftop arrays:** check the station's solar input limit first, because a station with a lower ceiling will bottleneck a large array. [Source](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)

## How to choose
- **Roof AC or induction cooktop:** you need roughly 3,000 W or more, so the R4000 or DELTA Pro 3. A 13,500 BTU AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup.
- **Fridge, lights, Starlink and laptop:** a 1–2 kWh unit is enough.
- **Wall charging between stops:** EcoFlow charges fastest, and Bluetti's older AC200P is slow.

The review sites' "Check price" buttons are affiliate links, and none of the other stations had a direct buy link in my results. Confirm current prices on each manufacturer's or retailer's page.

If you tell me your RV's biggest loads (especially whether you have a roof AC) and your roof or storage space, I can narrow this to one station and a panel count.
